correctness.rationale: Coarea reduces the norm of every constant-preserving linear operator to cut indicators; convexity of each cut output Gini in the independent rate vector sends global maxima to cube vertices. For a k-versus-m binary input and r selected/s unselected refreshed sites, direct three-level counting gives G(P1_S)=km+[ks(m-k-s)+mr(k-m-r)]/n. For k<=m the r-term is nonpositive and optimizing integer s yields floor((m-k)^2/4); parity-aware comparison across k proves k=1 is optimal, giving M_n=1+floor((n-2)^2/4)/[n(n-1)]. Singleton and endpoint rate witnesses attain the bound. Blending a maximizing rate vector with epsilon>0 uniform refresh gives an all-positive transition matrix and still has amplification if (1-epsilon)M_n>1. Correct n=2,3 equality, n>=4 amplification, and unattained n->infinity 5/4.
